content_text: [1/2 @gregoryblotnick] "Understanding Munger's Morality" -- ruthless pragmatism, non-dualistic thinking, and the virtues and vices of "The Eminent Dead." TIMESTAMPS: 0:00 - Introduction / What is Charlie Munger's Morality? 1:00 - "I’m not moral because it’s the right thing to do — but because it’s the best policy." + Munger: "It would be nice if I were Mother Teresa and did something I didn’t like doing because I am a noble soul, but my life is organized so that, time after time, what works for my pocketbook works for every moral teaching that I’ve been taught.” 2:00 - Schroeder dry snitching + Buffett's opaque morality 3:00 - Criticizing and praising Buffett: groupies versus critics 4:00 - Munger as a role model to my generation - for LIFE, not for investing. 5:00 - "how the world ACTUALLY works, not how its supposed to work" - Munger is unconstrained by morality and blind ideology 6:00 - core argument: virtues and vices, you can pick PIECEMEAL from individuals - no one is simply good or bad...the "arb" of human nature." 7:00 - the "real world" view of Munger - what do people criticize about him? 8:00 - the bear case on Buffett 9:00 - the objective view on Ben Franklin et al as pragmatists 10:00 - Munger's "Eminent Dead" + avoiding blind hero worship 11:00 - "not everyone should invest like Buffett, because not everyone is built like Buffett." 12:00 - the accordion of learning investors - zoom in, zoom out 13:00 - "God has never made a perfect man." 14:00 - To be continued / "the greatest gift is to help the next man think differently." --- [2/2 @gregoryblotnick] related material: https://x.com/gregoryblotnick/status/2090462442832769024?s=20
